overview: This Senate resolution designates February 23 through February 27, 2026, as "National Public Schools Week." Its preamble describes public schools as central to American communities and democracy, notes that most U.S. children attend them, and says lawmakers at every level should support strengthening them, along with services like counseling, after-school programs and mental health support. The resolution itself only makes the designation and does not change any law or funding. The Senate approved it on February 26, 2026.
for: Supporters say the resolution recognizes the teachers, principals and staff who educate most of the nation's children and calls attention to the value of public schools to local communities.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or spending, and some may feel it leaves out the many families who choose private schools or home schooling.
